subject: Redwood DPA — request to exclude Customer Data from model training
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@datacorp.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@datacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Redwood DPA — request to exclude Customer Data from model training

Hi Amy,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we discussed, DataCorp's security team asked our legal team to confirm whether Customer Data will be used to train Redwood models. I wanted to follow up with a short note and propose language so your counsel can see a concrete option.

High level: DataCorp is asking for an explicit carve-out in the DPA that prevents Redwood from using Customer Data for model training or similar model improvement. We're open to a narrow set of allowed operational uses (e.g., synthetic telemetry for availability/bugfixes, aggregated and de-identified metrics) but not raw-data training.

Proposed clause (for counsel review):
"Training Exclusion: 'Customer Data' shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning or generative models owned or operated by Redwood Inference, whether directly or indirectly, except that Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be re-identified for the limited purpose of monitoring service health, diagnosing issues, and maintaining system performance. Any other use of Customer Data for model training requires the Customer's prior written consent'"

A few other asks we expect from your side:
- Disclosure of subprocessors and 30-day notice for new subprocessors (we can share our current list — attached).
- Data transfer mechanism (SCCs or equivalent) if EU data involved (I assume not for this account but happy to confirm).
- Execution via DocuSign once language is agreed.

I've attached a redline of our standard DPA with the Training Exclusion inserted and a current subprocessors spreadsheet for your review. Can you let me know if this is a reasonable starting point for DataCorp legal, or share any counter-language they prefer?

If it's easier, we can set a 20-min alignment call with counsel today.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessors_2026-02-10.xlsx

From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@datacorp.com>

Cc: DataCorp Legal <legal@datacorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@datacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — request to exclude Customer Data from model training

Neha —

Thanks for the clear proposal and redlines. DataCorp's legal team reviewed the clause and the ask is generally reasonable, but we can't agree to a blanket prohibition without understanding operational exceptions. A few thoughts from Legal:

1) The 'aggregated, de-identified' carve-out you propose is promising, but Legal wants affirmative language that allows limited use for security and fraud detection, and also to de-bias models if that is required for safety. They also want the ability to require an auditor or independent expert to verify de-identification on an as-needed basis.

2) Regarding subprocessors: we need a standing commitment that Redwood will provide subprocessor notices 30 days prior to onboarding and an easy mechanism for DataCorp to object to specific subprocessors (with a short cure period).

3) Data transfer: we'll need confirmation you can support SCCs for EU data. For now DataCorp will treat the account as US-only, but we want the option to expand.

Could you have legal propose language that includes: (a) narrow allowed operational uses (security, fraud, system reliability), (b) an independent verifier clause limited to specific circumstances, and (c) the subprocessor notice/objection workflow?

Procurement is standing by to receive executed DPA + PO. If you can get a redline back by EOD, we can try to route it to our GC tomorrow.

Best,
Amy Chen
Senior Counsel, DataCorp
amy.chen@datacorp.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc:
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:22:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Redwood DPA — request to exclude Customer Data from model training

Laura / Vivek — forwarding DataCorp's response. They like the concept but want a few clarifications (independent verifier, slightly broader ops carve-outs, subprocessor objection rights). I've attached their note and our redline. Can legal propose a defensible clause that keeps the customer's restriction strong (no training on customer content without consent) but also allows Redwood to operate and maintain the service? Procurement wants quick turnaround — they asked for a redline by EOD and GC review tomorrow.

Quick context for drafting:
- We don't want language that prevents us from using aggregated telemetry for performance improvements.
- We should avoid giving a right to an open-ended external audit; propose an "independent expert" with narrow scope and confidentiality protections.
- For subprocessors, propose notice + cure (14 days) and if unresolved, a mitigation plan rather than immediate termination.

Thanks — Neha

Hi Amy / Neha,

Thanks for the constructive framing. I've attached a short redline of the DPA (see "Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf") with the following recommended language that I think balances the customer's privacy requirement and Redwood's operational needs. Key points:

- Training Exclusion (final text suggestion):
"Customer Data" shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models owned or operated by Redwood Inference, except as expressly permitted in this Section. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may process aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be re-identified for the limited purposes of (i) system reliability, (ii) security and fraud detection, and (iii) monitoring service health and availability. Any use of Customer Data for model training or model improvement beyond these limited purposes requires the Customer's prior written consent.

- Independent verifier: Redwood will permit, at Customer's expense, a single independent expert to assess whether used datasets are de-identified, subject to (a) reasonable scope and timing constraints, (b) a mutual NDA, and (c) protections against exposure of Customer Content. Redwood retains the right to select the expert from an agreed list and to request confidentiality and technical safeguards.

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and will accept written objections; in the event of an objection Redwood will work with Customer in good faith to propose a mitigation plan within 14 days. If mitigation is not reasonably achievable, parties may agree on termination rights specific to the impacted services.

- Data transfers: Redwood already supports SCCs and can work with DataCorp to implement them as part of execution.

If DataCorp is comfortable with this, we can produce a clean DPA and route it to DocuSign. If you need changes, please flag specific sentences.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Laura has suggested language (attached) that aligns with what you asked for while preserving the operational exceptions Redwood needs. The highlights:

- Narrow allowed uses (security, reliability, fraud detection) limited to aggregated/de-identified telemetry.
- Independent expert clause with NDA/confidentiality controls and Customer-paid engagements only.
- Subprocessor notice with 14-day mitigation plan and termination rights if unresolved.

I've attached the clean DPA with these edits. If this is acceptable, let me know and I'll send the DocuSign envelope for execution. Procurement mentioned they'll wait for the executed DPA + PO to kick off onboarding and billing.
